sections.body_md:
A mode is one piece of the free motion \(\dot x = Ax\). A real eigenvalue \(\lambda\) with eigenvector \(v\) contributes a multiple of \(e^{\lambda t} v\). The time constant of a decaying mode is the reciprocal of the absolute value of the real part. A complex conjugate pair contributes an oscillation at the imaginary part, inside an envelope set by the real part.

When a repeated eigenvalue has a full set of eigenvectors, each copy is still a pure exponential. When it does not, the matrix is not diagonalizable, and the missing direction brings a factor of \(t\) in front of \(e^{\lambda t}\). Computing the eigenvalues themselves is the previous skill. This skill reads the motion from an eigenvalue you already have.

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md: Free motion: \(x(t) = e^{At} x(0)\). When a full set of eigenvectors exists, \(A = V \Lambda V^{-1}\) and \[ e^{At} = V e^{\Lambda t} V^{-1}. \] A mode \(\sigma + j\omega\) decays at rate \(|\sigma|\) and oscillates at \(\omega\). Its time constant is \(1/|\sigma|\). A Jordan block for a repeated eigenvalue contributes an extra factor of \(t\).

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md: A real eigenvalue \(-6\) contributes \(e^{-6t}\). At one second the factor is \(e^{-6} = 0.0025\). The time constant of that mode is the reciprocal of 6. A complex pair \(-7 \pm j4\) decays at rate 7 and oscillates at 4 radians per second. The envelope time constant is the reciprocal of 7. The imaginary part is not the time constant. If \(-6\) were a double eigenvalue with only one eigenvector, the second solution would carry a factor of \(t\) and would not be another copy of \(e^{-6t}\).

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md:
- Reading the time constant from the imaginary part. The imaginary part is the oscillation.
- Treating a repeated eigenvalue as automatically diagonalizable. Count the independent eigenvectors.
- Dropping the factor of \(t\) in a Jordan block.
- Computing the matrix exponential entry by entry. Use \(V e^{\Lambda t} V^{-1}\) when the eigenvectors form a basis.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: Stability of a linear system asks whether every mode decays. Linearization reads the modes of a nonlinear system from the eigenvalues of its derivative at an equilibrium. An unobservable mode is one that does not appear in the output.
